    How it works

    In Settings, enter your Tarkov Market API key and click Save. The key is hidden by default; use the eye icon to show or hide it.

    Choose a game mode: PVP, PVE or SEASON. If you have multiple characters, select one. Item prices use the game mode of the selected character.

    Name scanning always uses English. Use English item names in the game and open the item's Inspect window. With Automatic scanning enabled, the app checks the title after a left-click while the game is in the foreground. It does not scan item names without an Inspect window.

    After clicking Scan now, switch back to the game within 3 seconds and keep the item's Inspect window open. Manual scanning also works when Automatic scanning is off.

    To search by name, enter the item's English name and click Search. This does not require an open Inspect window or Automatic scanning.

    Flea Market shows Best price and 24-hour average price. Trader shows the best trader price. The price per slot appears in parentheses. Trader prices use the trader's own currency.

    Items Tracker uses only Tarkov Market progress and appears when the selected character has an active mandatory requirement or remaining stock for the item. Filled requirements remain visible, for example 10/10, until the associated goal is completed. Refreshes keep the loaded panel visible while data updates in the background; stock actions pause until the refresh finishes. The Add item button and shortcut stop adding when no eligible requirement needs another item.

    Stock always shows available stock / required quantity, for example 2/5. When the collection target is covered and no other item requirement remains, Stock shows your available stock as complete, for example 2/2 or 0/0. Found in Raid and Regular requirements appear on separate rows, but share the same stock.

    Shared and Shared (FiR) show the latest group progress confirmed by Tarkov Market, including stock from other eligible items. Stock includes pending additions and removals immediately; Shared progress updates after the API confirms it. The collection target takes other eligible items into account without subtracting the selected item's own stock twice.

    Click Add item or press F1 to add one item to the selected character's shared stock. Click Remove item or press F2 to remove one item when stock is available. Found in Raid and Regular labels describe the API requirements; adding does not assign an item quality. Each shortcut works while the game is in the foreground, but only when the loaded item's corresponding button is available. Each physical press changes stock by at most one item; holding the key does not repeat. Stock changes immediately while the update is sent to Tarkov Market in the background. The status log shows how many stock changes are waiting for the API save. A rejected update restores the confirmed stock. Network errors keep pending changes in memory; uncertain saves are checked before retrying. Pending updates are kept only while the app runs; closing with unsaved items shows a warning.

    F1 adds and F2 removes by default. Change each shortcut separately in Settings, or use Disable to release it. While enabled, the keys are reserved globally for normal Windows keyboard input even when the corresponding stock action is unavailable. Apps that use direct keyboard input may still receive the keys.

    Completed quest and hideout requirements appear on separate rows, for example 4 items completed. These quantities indicate completion and do not increase stock.

    Text recognition runs locally on screenshots. The app does not read or modify the game's memory and does not send screenshots to external services. Item prices and data come from the Tarkov Market API.

    Closing either app window closes both windows.
